title: Preterite — Regular Verbs
description: Master regular preterite conjugations for -AR, -ER, and -IR verbs to tell stories about the past.

grammar.title: Preterite (Pretérito Indefinido) — Regular Verbs
grammar.content:
The preterite tense is used to talk about completed actions in the past with a clear beginning or end. Think of it as the 'storytelling' tense — you're telling someone what happened.

For regular -AR verbs (like hablar), the endings are:
- yo: -é
- tú: -aste
- él/ella/usted: -ó
- nosotros: -amos
- vosotros: -asteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -aron

For regular -ER/-IR verbs (like comer, vivir), the endings are:
- yo: -í
- tú: -iste
- él/ella/usted: -ió
- nosotros: -imos
- vosotros: -isteis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -ieron
examples: Ayer hablé con mi amigo. (Yesterday I talked with my friend.)
Ellos comieron pizza anoche. (They ate pizza last night.)
Nosotros vivimos en Madrid dos años. (We lived in Madrid for two years.)
¿Estudiaste para el examen? (Did you study for the exam?)
grammar.aid_note: Watch out: 'nosotros' form looks the same for -AR preterite and present! Context tells you which: 'hablamos' in present = we speak; 'hablamos' in preterite = we spoke. Look for time words like 'ayer' (yesterday), 'la semana pasada' (last week).

pronunciation.title: Stress and Accents in the Preterite
pronunciation.content:
The preterite tense has accent marks on several forms that are critical for correct pronunciation:

- yo -AR: hablÉ, trabajÉ, estudiÉ (always accent on the -é)
- tú -ER/-IR: comISTE, vivISTE (stress on the second-to-last syllable — no accent needed)
- él/ella -AR: hablÓ, trabajÓ (always accent on the -ó)
- él/ella -ER/-IR: comIÓ, vivIÓ (always accent on the -ió)

The nosotros form for -AR verbs (hablamos) has NO accent — this is what makes it look identical to the present tense.

The ellos/ellas form for all verbs (hablaron, comieron, vivieron) has NO accent — the stress falls naturally on the second-to-last syllable.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian doesn't use written accents on verbs the same way Spanish does, but the stress pattern is similar. Remember: Spanish preterite yo and él/ella forms always carry an accent mark.

exercises.question: What is the preterite form of 'hablar' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hablé' is the yo form of hablar in the preterite. The -é ending marks first-person singular preterite for -AR verbs.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Nosotros ____ (comer) pizza anoche.' (We ate pizza last night.)
exercises.explanation: 'Comimos' is the nosotros form of comer in the preterite. -IR ending for -ER verb nosotros.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Ella ____ (escribir) una carta ayer.' (She wrote a letter yesterday.)
exercises.explanation: 'Escribió' is the él/ella/usted preterite of escribir. -IR verbs get -ió in the third person: escribiÓ.

exercises.question: Complete the preterite tense conjugation table for regular -AR verb HABLAR:
exercises.explanation: Regular -AR preterite: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron.

exercises.question: Complete the preterite tense conjugation table for regular -ER verb COMER:
exercises.explanation: Regular -ER preterite: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the preterite correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Ayer hablé' uses the preterite for a completed past action. 'Hablo' = present, 'hablaba' = imperfect, 'hablaré' = future.

exercises.question: Complete: '¿____ (estudiar) tú para el examen?' (Did you study for the exam?)
exercises.explanation: 'Estudiaste' is the tú form of estudiar in the preterite. -AR verbs get -aste for tú: estudiaste.
